v2:c189b2effda222513ad757a2ec33bb512ab56.key: The "is the narrative just a restatement of the tabular features?" objection has a mature, largely closed literature behind it, and the paper must cite it rather than invent a solution. Three separate families exist and they answer three different questions: (a) residualisation / partialling out (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell, Robinson 1988, Chernozhukov et al. 2018 DML) removes the linear-in-nuisance part of the text channel and gives a coefficient with a defensible interpretation; (b) concept erasure (INLP, R-LACE, LEACE, kernelised erasure) gives a *provable* guarantee, but only against a stated adversary class (linear, log-linear, a fixed kernel) — LEACE is closed-form, optimal in the linear case, and is the single citation a 2026 paper cannot omit; (c) conditional independence testing (model-X knockoffs, HRT, CPI) is the only family that actually tests the reviewer's hypothesis, H0: choice ⊥ narrative | observed attributes, and yields a p-value rather than a delta-NLL. The strongest, cheapest revision is: (1) apply LEACE to the sentence embedding with respect to the tabular attribute vector, per-alternative, before it enters the utility; report the ablation with and without erasure; (2) run an HRT/CPI conditional independence test on a held-out split to get a p-value that the narrative channel adds information beyond the observed attributes; (3) cite the concept-leakage literature (Mahinpei et al. 2021; Havasi et al. 2022) explicitly, because it is exactly the failure mode the reviewer is naming for an interpretable bottleneck. None of (1)-(3) can be sold as novel machinery; the novelty must sit in the choice-model formulation (outcome-mediated utility with a provably-orthogonal semantic channel, and the behavioural claim that the orthogonal residual is interpretable as perceived outcome), not in the orthogonality technique.

papers.title: Partial Time Regressions as Compared with Individual Trends
papers.relevance: Frisch & Waugh. Origin of the partialling-out result: a coefficient in a multiple regression equals the coefficient from regressing the residualised outcome on the residualised regressor.
papers.implication: The baseline formalism for 'the text channel only gets the variation the tabular attributes cannot explain'. Cite as the ancestor; never present residualisation as a contribution.

papers.title: Seasonal Adjustment of Economic Time Series and Multiple Regression Analysis
papers.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 58(304), 993-1010
papers.relevance: Lovell. Generalises Frisch-Waugh to arbitrary multivariate conditioning sets using projection matrices; this is the form actually usable when the nuisance set is a whole attribute vector per alternative.
papers.implication: Gives the exact projection you would apply to the per-alternative sentence embedding: M = I - X(X'X)^{-1}X' with X the observed attribute matrix. This is a two-line method section, which is precisely why it cannot be a claimed novelty.

papers.title: Root-N-Consistent Semiparametric Regression
papers.relevance: Robinson. The partially linear model Y = beta'X + phi(Z) + e, estimated by double residualisation: regress Y on Z and X on Z nonparametrically, then regress residual on residual.
papers.implication: Exactly the structure of OM-LEU if you treat the observed attributes as the nuisance Z and the narrative-derived utility term as the target. Estimating the semantic coefficient on doubly-residualised quantities makes the claim 'this is not a restatement' an estimation property rather than an empirical hope.

papers.title: Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters
papers.relevance: Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Demirer, Duflo, Hansen, Newey, Robins. Neyman-orthogonal scores plus cross-fitting so that a flexible ML nuisance estimator does not bias the low-dimensional parameter of interest.
papers.implication: The modern version of the fix: the tabular channel is the nuisance, learned by whatever model you like, and the narrative coefficient is estimated on cross-fitted residuals. Cross-fitting also answers the reviewer's separate worry that the gain is a fitting artefact of the amplified observed-attribute channel — without cross-fitting, a flexible tabular channel overfits and the semantic channel picks up its residual error.

papers.title: Null It Out: Guarding Protected Attributes by Iterative Nullspace Projection
papers.relevance: Ravfogel, Elazar, Gonen, Twiton, Goldberg. INLP: repeatedly fit a linear probe for the concept and project onto its nullspace until no linear probe succeeds.
papers.implication: The first thing a reviewer will ask for as a baseline erasure method, and the reason a 2026 paper cannot call projection-based removal new. Worth citing as superseded by LEACE rather than used.

papers.title: Linear Adversarial Concept Erasure
papers.relevance: Ravfogel, Twiton, Goldberg, Cotterell. R-LACE: formulates erasure as a constrained linear minimax game and finds a low-rank orthogonal projection that provably blocks linear recovery.
papers.implication: Relevant if you want to remove only a low-rank tabular subspace from the text channel rather than the full attribute span, which preserves more semantic signal. Its rank-k formulation gives a natural knob for the ablation table: performance as a function of how much of the tabular subspace is erased.

papers.title: Kernelized Concept Erasure
papers.relevance: Ravfogel, Vargas, Goldberg, Cotterell. Kernelises the erasure objective to block nonlinear adversaries; finds that protection does not transfer across different nonlinear adversaries.
papers.implication: This is the honest caveat the revision must state. If the narrative is orthogonalised only against linear functions of the attributes, a nonlinear restatement of the attributes could still survive, and this paper shows exhaustive nonlinear erasure is unsolved. Cite it to pre-empt the obvious follow-up objection rather than let a reviewer raise it.

papers.title: LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36)
papers.relevance: Belrose, Schneider-Joseph, Ravfogel, Cotterell, Raff, Biderman. Closed-form affine transform that provably prevents every linear classifier from recovering the concept while minimally perturbing the representation under a broad class of norms.
papers.implication: The single most load-bearing citation for this revision. Applied to the per-alternative sentence embedding with the observed attribute vector as the 'concept', it makes 'the narrative channel is not a linear restatement of the observed attributes' a theorem, not an ablation. It is closed-form, so it costs one matrix computation and does not disturb the training recipe. It also handles continuous, multi-dimensional targets, which the attribute vector is.

papers.title: Log-linear Guardedness and its Implications
papers.relevance: Ravfogel, Goldberg, Cotterell. Shows that linear guardedness does not imply a downstream multiclass log-linear model cannot indirectly recover the erased concept.
papers.implication: Directly relevant because a choice model IS a multiclass log-linear model over alternatives. Erasing the attributes linearly from the embedding does not by itself guarantee the softmax over alternatives cannot reconstruct them. The revision must engage with this or the 'provable' claim overreaches; the safe framing is 'provably not linearly recoverable', with the conditional-independence test carrying the stronger empirical claim.

papers.title: The Medium Is Not the Message: Deconfounding Document Embeddings via Linear Concept Erasure
papers.relevance: Fan, Tian, Ravfogel, Sachan, Ash, Hoyle. Applies LEACE-style linear erasure to strip confounders (source, language) from document embeddings; finds confounders are encoded near-linearly even in highly nonlinear encoders, and that erasure does not degrade downstream quality.
papers.implication: The closest existing precedent for exactly the operation this paper needs, and evidence that the cost is low. It is also a warning: an applied 'erase confounders from text embeddings' contribution already exists in 2025, so the revision cannot frame the erasure itself as the contribution.

papers.title: Adversarial Removal of Demographic Attributes from Text Data
papers.relevance: Elazar & Goldberg. Shows an adversarially 'cleaned' representation still permits a post-hoc classifier to recover the attribute.
papers.implication: The reason not to build the revision on an adversarial independence head alone. Cite when explaining why you chose a closed-form, certifiable projection over an adversarial penalty.

papers.title: Domain-Adversarial Training of Neural Networks
papers.relevance: Ganin, Ustinova, Ajakan, Germain, Larochelle, Laviolette, Marchand, Lempitsky. Gradient reversal layer for training a representation from which a discriminator cannot predict a nuisance variable.
papers.implication: The default adversarial-independence mechanism. Applicable as the 'soft' variant: a discriminator that tries to predict tabular attributes from the semantic channel, with reversed gradients. Standard enough that it is a baseline, not a method.

papers.title: Learning to Pivot with Adversarial Networks
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2017 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30)
papers.relevance: Louppe, Kagan, Cranmer. Adversarial training with a theoretical result that the optimum is a pivotal quantity, i.e. genuinely independent of continuous nuisance parameters.
papers.implication: The right citation if you use an adversarial penalty against continuous tabular attributes (price, duration, rating), because it handles the continuous case with a stated optimality condition rather than heuristically.

papers.title: Measuring Statistical Dependence with Hilbert-Schmidt Norms
papers.relevance: Gretton, Bousquet, Smola, Schölkopf. Introduces HSIC, a kernel dependence measure that is zero if and only if the variables are independent (for characteristic kernels), and is estimable from samples without density estimation.
papers.implication: The penalty form for nonlinear non-redundancy: add lambda * HSIC(semantic utility term, attribute vector) to the loss. Unlike a linear projection it targets all dependence, not just linear. Its measured value also gives a reportable number for 'how much of the narrative is attribute restatement' as training proceeds.

papers.title: Kernel dependence regularizers and Gaussian processes with applications to algorithmic fairness
papers.relevance: Pérez-Suay, Adsuara, Piles, Martínez-Ferrer, Díaz, Muñoz-Marí, Camps-Valls. Formalises HSIC and normalised-HSIC as regularisers inside regularised empirical risk minimisation over RKHS.
papers.implication: The citable form of 'HSIC as a training penalty' rather than as a test statistic. Use it to justify the penalty term; do not present the penalty as new.

papers.title: Domain Separation Networks
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2016 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 29)
papers.relevance: Bousmalis, Trigeorgis, Silberman, Krishnan, Erhan. Explicitly partitions a representation into shared and private subspaces with a soft orthogonality constraint plus a reconstruction loss; ablation shows removing the orthogonality constraint consistently hurts.
papers.implication: The architectural precedent for 'one channel carries what the other cannot'. The reconstruction loss matters: without it, the orthogonal private channel collapses to noise. That is the mechanism your Amazon result may be missing, and the DSN ablation is the template for the knock-out table the reviewer is asking for.

papers.title: MISA: Modality-Invariant and -Specific Representations for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
papers.relevance: Hazarika, Zimmermann, Poria. Per-modality projection into a shared subspace and a private subspace, trained with a combination of distributional similarity, orthogonality, reconstruction and task losses.
papers.implication: The most direct multi-view analogue of a tabular channel plus a text channel in a fusion model. It establishes that 'orthogonal private channel + shared channel + reconstruction' is a known recipe in multimodal learning, so the contribution has to be the choice-theoretic reading of the private channel, not the decomposition.

papers.title: Barlow Twins: Self-Supervised Learning via Redundancy Reduction
papers.relevance: Zbontar, Jing, Misra, LeCun, Deny. Drives the cross-correlation matrix between two representations toward the identity, penalising off-diagonal redundancy.
papers.implication: A cheap, batch-level decorrelation objective between the semantic channel's dimensions and the tabular feature dimensions. Useful as a lightweight regulariser and as a reported redundancy diagnostic (off-diagonal mass), but it is a well-known objective.

papers.title: Deep Canonical Correlation Analysis
papers.relevance: Andrew, Arora, Bilmes, Livescu. Learns nonlinear transformations of two views maximising their correlation.
papers.implication: The inverse measurement: fit DCCA between the sentence embeddings and the tabular attributes, and report the canonical correlations. High canonical correlation is quantitative evidence that the narratives are semantic expansions of the observed features; the residual directions with low correlation are the part that could carry perceived outcome. This turns the reviewer's qualitative doubt into a number you control.

papers.title: Panning for gold: 'model-X' knockoffs for high dimensional controlled variable selection
papers.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 80(3), 551-577
papers.relevance: Candès, Fan, Janson, Lv. Finite-sample valid inference for conditional independence of a covariate and the response given all other covariates, with no assumption on the conditional law of the response.
papers.implication: The correct formal statement of the reviewer's question: test H0 that the choice is independent of the narrative channel given the observed attributes. If you can reject this on a held-out split, 'not a restatement' stops being an ablation argument and becomes a hypothesis test with error control.

papers.title: The Holdout Randomization Test for Feature Selection in Black Box Models
papers.venue: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 31(1), 151-162
papers.relevance: Tansey, Veitch, Zhang, Rabadan, Blei. A data-splitting conditional randomization test that produces a valid p-value per feature using any fitted black-box predictor, without retraining.
papers.implication: The most practical version to actually run here. Fit OM-LEU once, then on a holdout resample the narrative channel from its conditional distribution given the observed attributes and recompute the choice likelihood; the p-value quantifies the narrative's conditional contribution. This is a single extra experiment and it addresses the reviewer's strongest point directly.

papers.title: Testing conditional independence in supervised learning algorithms
papers.relevance: Watson & Wright. The conditional predictive impact (CPI): an unbiased estimator of a feature group's contribution conditional on a reduced feature set, with inference procedures, working with any learner and loss.
papers.implication: Gives a signed, interpretable effect size with confidence intervals for 'how much does the narrative channel add on top of the observed attributes', in the model's own loss units (log-likelihood). This is the number that replaces the contested delta-NLL table; report it per dataset, and especially for Amazon where the reviewer suspects the gain is the amplified attribute channel.

papers.title: Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.relevance: Koh, Nguyen, Tang, Mussmann, Pierson, Kim, Liang. Predict human-specified concepts first, then predict the label from the concepts, enabling test-time intervention on concepts.
papers.implication: The architecture the reviewer means by 'interpretable bottleneck-style'. Must be cited as the frame, and the revision needs a stated difference: CBM concepts are supervised and human-labelled, whereas the perceived-outcome narratives are unsupervised and unverified, which is precisely why an orthogonality guarantee is needed here and not there.

papers.title: Promises and Pitfalls of Black-Box Concept Learning Models
papers.venue: arXiv:2106.13314; ICML 2021 Workshop on Theoretic Foundation, Criticism, and Application Trend of Explainable AI
papers.relevance: Mahinpei, Clark, Lage, Doshi-Velez, Pan. Documents concept leakage: soft concept representations encode information beyond their nominal semantics, and the task head exploits it, so the bottleneck is not doing the interpretive work it claims.
papers.implication: This is the reviewer's objection stated in the concept-learning literature's own vocabulary. The revision should name it as the failure mode being guarded against, which reframes the orthogonality machinery as a principled response to a known problem rather than an ad hoc patch.

papers.title: Addressing Leakage in Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2022 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35)
papers.relevance: Havasi, Parbhoo, Doshi-Velez. Diagnoses leakage in CBMs and proposes fixes including a side channel and an autoregressive concept structure.
papers.implication: Shows the accepted remedy for leakage is an explicit side channel plus structure, not merely a penalty. Maps onto a design where the observed attributes get their own unconstrained channel and the narrative channel is constrained to be orthogonal to it, which is a cleaner story than the current amplified-attribute channel.

papers.title: Concept whitening for interpretable image recognition
papers.relevance: Chen, Bei, Rudin. Replaces batch normalisation with a whitening plus rotation module so latent axes are decorrelated and aligned to known concepts.
papers.implication: Prior art for building decorrelation into the interpretable layer rather than adding a penalty. Relevant if the semantic channel is a fixed-width bottleneck: whiten it against the tabular attribute directions so each retained axis is by construction non-redundant.

papers.title: Text as Data
papers.relevance: Gentzkow, Kelly, Taddy. Survey of using text as an input in economic research, including the statistical treatment of high-dimensional text covariates alongside structured ones.
papers.implication: The right citation for the audience framing: a choice model with a text channel is a text-as-data exercise, and this survey sets the expectation that the text's incremental contribution over structured covariates be argued, not assumed. Useful for positioning against econometric reviewers.

already_standard: Residualisation / partialling out (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell, Lovell 1963). Regressing one channel on another and keeping the residual is textbook econometrics. It can be used but must be cited as FWL; presenting it as a method contribution would be a straightforward novelty failure.

Double machine learning with cross-fitting (Chernozhukov et al. 2018) and the partially linear double-residual estimator (Robinson 1988). Standard since 2018; the DoubleML software is mature. Cite and use, do not claim.

Linear concept erasure by nullspace projection (INLP, 2020) and its closed-form optimal successor (LEACE, NeurIPS 2023). LEACE in particular is the known best answer to 'make this representation linearly uninformative about that variable'. A 2026 paper that performs linear erasure without citing LEACE will be read as unaware of the field.

Adversarial independence via gradient reversal (Ganin et al. 2016) and pivotal adversarial training (Louppe et al. 2017). These are default baselines, and Elazar & Goldberg (2018) already established they under-deliver, so an adversarial penalty alone is neither novel nor convincing.
HSIC as an independence penalty in a training objective (Gretton et al. 2005 for the criterion; Pérez-Suay et al. 2022 for the regulariser form). Widely used in fairness and representation learning.

Shared/private subspace decomposition with an orthogonality constraint plus reconstruction loss (Domain Separation Networks 2016; MISA 2020). The exact architecture of 'a channel that carries what the other channel cannot' already exists in domain adaptation and multimodal fusion.
Redundancy reduction by driving a cross-correlation matrix to the identity (Barlow Twins, ICML 2021).

Conditional independence testing for 'does feature group A add anything given feature group B': model-X knockoffs (JRSS-B 2018), the holdout randomization test (JCGS 2021) and the conditional predictive impact (Machine Learning 2021). These are the established statistical instruments; using one is good practice, inventing a bespoke redundancy score instead would be a weakness.

The concept-bottleneck frame itself (Koh et al. ICML 2020) and the leakage critique of it (Mahinpei et al. 2021; Havasi et al. NeurIPS 2022). The reviewer's second and third concerns are literally the leakage literature, so it must appear in the related work.

Applying linear erasure to text embeddings to remove an observed confounder is now itself published applied work (Fan et al., EMNLP 2025), which closes off 'we erase confounders from LLM text features' as a standalone claim.
genuinely_open: Nonlinear erasure with a guarantee. Kernelized Concept Erasure (EMNLP 2022) reports that protection against one nonlinear adversary does not transfer to another, and states exhaustive removal of a nonlinearly encoded concept is unsolved. So 'the narrative is provably not a nonlinear restatement of the observed attributes' is not currently achievable, and any claim in the paper must be scoped to linear (or a stated kernel) recoverability.

Erasure guarantees that survive a downstream log-linear head. Log-linear Guardedness (ACL 2023) shows a multiclass softmax can indirectly recover a linearly-erased concept. Since a discrete choice model IS a softmax over alternatives, whether linear erasure at the embedding level implies non-redundancy at the utility level is an open question, and one this paper is unusually well placed to study.

Erasure under a per-alternative, per-decision structure. All the erasure literature operates on a single flat representation. Choice data has an alternative dimension, a chooser dimension and an attribute vector that varies within a choice set. What the correct conditioning set is (erase against this alternative's attributes, against all alternatives in the set, against attribute differences within the set) is not settled anywhere, and differences-within-choice-set is what actually enters a logit utility. This is a real methodological opening.

Preserving task-relevant signal while erasing. Erasure minimises representation change under a norm, not under downstream utility. How to erase the attribute-redundant part of a narrative while provably retaining the perceived-outcome part is not solved; the trade-off curve (erasure rank vs. predictive gain) is itself a publishable empirical object.

Distinguishing 'perceived outcome' from 'semantic expansion' as a construct, not just as orthogonality. Orthogonality shows the channel is not a restatement; it does not show the channel is a perceived outcome. Establishing that requires external validation, for example against stated-preference or satisfaction data, or intervention experiments where the narrative is edited and the predicted choice changes in the direction behavioural theory predicts. No existing paper does this for LLM-generated narratives in a choice model.

Whether LLM-generated narratives carry information the tabular attributes lack at all, tested rather than ablated. The tabular-LLM literature asserts embeddings 'add signal' but conditional-independence testing of that claim on choice data is essentially absent, so running an HRT or CPI on this question is a genuine empirical contribution even though the tools are standard.

Calibration versus information. Your own uniform-floor control already separates these; the literature has no accepted protocol for reporting how much of a text channel's log-likelihood gain is calibration rather than new information. Formalising that split would answer the 'gains depend on the amplified observed-attribute channel' objection in a way that generalises beyond this paper.
v2:c189b2effda222513ad757a2ec33bb512ab56.verdict: The orthogonality machinery cannot carry the novelty claim: residualisation is from 1933, DML from 2018, LEACE from 2023, HSIC penalties and shared/private orthogonal subspaces are standard, and applying linear erasure to text embeddings to remove an observed confounder was published at EMNLP 2025. Any framing of the revision as "we propose a new method for making a text channel non-redundant" will be rejected on the same novelty ground the reviewer already raised. What is defensible is narrower and stronger. First, adopt LEACE (closed form, one matrix, no training-recipe change) to make "the narrative channel is not a linear restatement of the observed attributes" a stated guarantee rather than an ablation argument, and report the erased-vs-unerased comparison as the headline table. Second, add a conditional independence test (HRT is the cheapest: refit nothing, resample the narrative channel given the attributes on a holdout, recompute choice likelihood; CPI if you want a signed effect size with a confidence interval) so the "does it add anything beyond the features" question is answered with a p-value on every dataset, Amazon included. Third, cite the concept-leakage line (Mahinpei 2021, Havasi 2022) by name and restructure so the observed attributes get an explicit unconstrained side channel while the narrative channel is constrained orthogonal to it, which is the accepted remedy and directly dissolves the "gains depend on the amplified observed-attribute channel" objection by construction. The novel contribution then has to be stated at the choice-model level, and there are three openings that are genuinely unclaimed: (i) what the correct conditioning set is for erasure under a choice-set structure, where within-set attribute differences rather than raw levels enter the utility, and no existing erasure paper addresses this; (ii) whether linear guardedness at the embedding survives a multinomial-logit head, which Log-linear Guardedness (ACL 2023) says is not implied and which this paper is uniquely positioned to test; (iii) validating "perceived outcome" as a construct rather than merely as an orthogonal residual, via narrative-intervention experiments where edited narratives move predicted choice in theory-predicted directions. Be explicit about the limit: honestly scope the claim to linear (or stated-kernel) non-recoverability, because the nonlinear case is open per Kernelized Concept Erasure, and a scoped claim with a citation reads as command of the literature while an unscoped one invites the next reviewer to break it.

papers.title: TabLLM: Few-shot Classification of Tabular Data with Large Language Models
papers.relevance: RAN A MATCHED-INFORMATION CONTROL — and it is the single closest precedent to your proposed 'template control'. Hegselmann et al. compared nine serializations of the SAME tabular row: List Template, Text Template ('The {column} is {value}'), Table-To-Text, Text T0 (LLM-generated prose), Text GPT-3 (GPT-3 rewriting the row as natural text), plus List-Only-Values, List-Permuted-Names, List-Permuted-Values, List-Short. The last three are information-destroying placebo controls in the exact sense the reviewer wants.
papers.implication: The hand-written Text Template beat both LLM-generated serializations in zero- and few-shot settings; the paper attributes this to hallucination ('GPT-3 added "this car is a good choice" or added entirely new data') and to LLMs not faithfully including all features. You CANNOT claim a template control as novel in 2026 — it is three years old and in a well-cited paper. Worse, the known result is that LLM prose loses to a template on identical fields, so you must run it and report it honestly, not present it as a contribution. Frame it as 'we apply the TabLLM-style serialization control to outcome narratives' and make the CONTRIBUTION the finding (narratives beat the matched template by X nats), not the control.

papers.title: Waffling around for Performance: Visual Classification with Random Words and Broad Concepts
papers.relevance: RAN THE PLACEBO CONTROL, and it is the canonical negative result of this whole genre. Roth, Kim, Koepke, Vinyals, Schmid, Akata replaced LLM-generated class descriptors with RANDOM character strings and random words and recovered comparable gains across many benchmarks.
papers.implication: This is the paper a hostile reviewer will cite against you. It establishes that gains attributed to 'LLM semantic knowledge' can come from ensembling/averaging over many text variants rather than from content. Your K outcome narratives per alternative, averaged via salience, is structurally the same averaging-over-descriptors mechanism. You need a WaffleCLIP-style control: K random/shuffled narratives at matched count and length. If OM-LEU survives it, that is a real result; if you do not run it, the reviewer's 'semantic expansion' concern stands unanswered.

papers.title: Visual Classification via Description from Large Language Models
papers.relevance: The positive claim that WaffleCLIP overturned. Menon & Vondrick prompt an LLM for descriptive attributes per class and classify by scoring those descriptors — the direct visual ancestor of 'prompt an LLM for consequences per alternative, then score them on a semantic basis'. NO matched-information control.
papers.implication: Cite it as the structural precursor of your outcome-generation step and acknowledge that it did not isolate semantic content. Your novelty cannot be 'we generate descriptions and score them'; that is ICLR 2023.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Automated Data Science: Introducing CAAFE for Context-Aware Automated Feature Engineering
papers.relevance: The reference point for LLM-generated features on tabular data. Hollmann, Müller, Hutter: LLM iteratively writes Python creating semantically meaningful columns from a dataset description; mean ROC AUC 0.798 to 0.822 on 11/14 datasets. NO matched-information control — baseline is no-feature-engineering, not a template rendering of the same fields.
papers.implication: Establishes 'LLM-generated features help tabular prediction' as prior art, so that claim is not yours. It also shares your exact unaddressed weakness, which is useful rhetorically: the field's flagship paper did not isolate the contribution either.

papers.title: ELF-Gym: Evaluating Large Language Models Generated Features for Tabular Prediction
papers.relevance: PARTIAL MATCHED-INFORMATION CONTROL. Evaluates LLM-generated features against expert-designed 'golden' features from Kaggle-winning solutions, measuring semantic and functional overlap rather than only downstream accuracy. Finds LLMs capture at best roughly two-thirds of expert features, and that strong feature-recall does not imply downstream gain (GPT-4o generated more features and performed worse downstream).
papers.implication: Gives you a citable, pre-existing methodology for 'are these features new information or restatements'. Use its recall/overlap framing to measure how much of an outcome narrative is recoverable from the tabular fields it was generated from. Also gives you a documented dissociation between semantic quality and predictive gain — which is precisely the reviewer's point about the Amazon results.

papers.title: Large Language Models Engineer Too Many Simple Features For Tabular Data
papers.relevance: NEGATIVE RESULT. Küken, Purucker, Hutter evaluate four LLMs across 27 tabular datasets and show a strong bias toward simple operators (addition) and failure to use compositional ones (group-by-then-aggregate), which degrades downstream predictive performance.
papers.implication: Direct evidence that LLM-generated features are systematically shallow recombinations of inputs. Supports the reviewer's 'semantic expansion, not new information' hypothesis as a live, documented failure mode you must rule out rather than assert away.

papers.title: Multi-level Diagnosis and Evaluation for Robust Tabular Feature Engineering with Large Language Models
papers.relevance: Three-level diagnostic: does the LLM identify the right variables (golden variable), the right directionality (golden relation), and the right thresholds (golden value). Gains up to 10.52 percent AUC only AFTER filtering by a Reliability Score; robustness varies sharply by dataset.
papers.implication: A ready-made auditing protocol you can adapt to ask whether generated consequences encode decision-relevant structure or restate attributes. Also documents high variance across datasets, which is the most defensible framing for your Amazon-vs-Mobility asymmetry.

papers.title: LLM-FE: Automated Feature Engineering for Tabular Data with LLMs as Evolutionary Optimizers
papers.relevance: RAN A SEMANTICS-ABLATION CONTROL. When dataset/task descriptions are removed from the prompt and feature names are anonymized with generic placeholders, performance drops substantially (reported to 0.626), isolating how much of the gain is prior knowledge versus data-driven search. Also reports a negative correlation between the LLM's familiarity with a dataset and the size of the gain.
papers.implication: The anonymization ablation is a second, complementary control that is already standard. For OM-LEU: regenerate outcomes with column names and product/category names masked. If performance holds, the narratives are doing structural work; if it collapses, the channel is world-knowledge lookup. The familiarity-versus-gain correlation also gives you a contamination check for Amazon.

papers.title: Elephants Never Forget: Memorization and Learning of Tabular Data in Large Language Models
papers.relevance: Bordt, Nori, Rodrigues, Nushi, Caruana show LLMs have memorized many popular tabular datasets verbatim and perform better on datasets seen during training, invalidating downstream evaluation.
papers.implication: Essential for Amazon. Amazon review/metadata corpora are heavily represented in pretraining. A reviewer can argue your outcome narratives leak memorized product knowledge or even co-purchase structure. Run their contamination tests (header/row-completion) on your Amazon fixture and report the result; this is cheap and pre-empts a rejection reason.

papers.title: End-to-end Training for Recommendation with Language-based User Profiles (LangPTune)
papers.relevance: RAN THE EXACT MATCHED-INFORMATION CONTROL AND GOT A NEGATIVE RESULT. Their 'NoProfile' baseline feeds the raw list of item metadata — the same information the LLM profile was generated from — into the same architecture. NoProfile-CL reached Recall@20 0.1012 / NDCG@20 0.0543 versus LangPTune's 0.0970 / 0.0494. The LLM-generated natural-language profile was WORSE than the raw fields it summarised.
papers.implication: The strongest single precedent for the reviewer's concern, and also your best template for how to handle it. They defended the method on interpretability grounds while conceding the information loss ('profiles are shorter and more concise'). OM-LEU can make the same honest move, but only if the outcome channel actually wins on NLL once the observed-attribute channel is held fixed. This paper proves the control is standard practice and that publishable papers report losing it.

papers.title: LLM-Rec: Personalized Recommendation via Prompting Large Language Models

papers.title: The Impact of Placebic Explanations on Trust in Intelligent Systems
papers.relevance: Eiband, Buschek, Kremer, Hussmann: lab study, 30 participants, three conditions (no explanation / PLACEBIC explanation / real explanation). Placebic explanations, which convey no information, invoked perceived trust similar to real explanations.
papers.implication: The intellectual origin of the placebo-text control, predating LLMs by four years. Cite it to establish that a content-free control is a long-standing methodological norm — which settles the question: proposing one in 2026 is good practice, never a contribution.

already_standard: Prompting an LLM to expand structured records into natural-language descriptions and feeding the text or its embeddings to a downstream predictor. Established by TabLLM (AISTATS 2023) and CAAFE (NeurIPS 2023); routine by 2024. Cannot be claimed as novel.

LLM-generated descriptors/concepts scored and aggregated into an interpretable prediction. Menon & Vondrick (ICLR 2023) for vision; Feng et al. BC-LLM (NeurIPS 2025) for the Bayesian version. Your 'prompt-defined semantic basis + learned scores' is this pattern.

The TEMPLATE CONTROL itself — comparing LLM-generated prose against a deterministic template rendering of the identical fields. TabLLM did exactly this in 2023 across nine serializations and found the template WON. It is three-year-old standard practice and, worse, the known direction of the result runs against you.

PLACEBO / RANDOM-TEXT CONTROLS — random word descriptors (WaffleCLIP, ICCV 2023), random phrase concepts in the CBM literature, random joint embeddings (A-LLMRec, KDD 2024), shuffled embeddings. Standard and expected.
THE 'NO-LLM RICHER SIDE INFORMATION' CONTROL — feeding the raw metadata the profile was generated from into the same backbone. LangPTune (2024) ran it as 'NoProfile' and the LLM profile lost.

SEMANTICS-ABLATION BY ANONYMIZATION — masking column names / entity names with opaque identifiers to separate world knowledge from data-driven structure. LLM-FE (2025) and From Residuals to Reasons (2026) both run it.
CONTAMINATION / MEMORIZATION CHECKS before claiming LLM knowledge helps on a public dataset. Bordt et al., COLM 2024. Expected for any Amazon-based result.

RESIDUAL-ANCHORED LLM AUGMENTATION — fit a base model, ask the LLM only what the base model is missing. Published prior art as of May 2026 (From Residuals to Reasons). This is now competition for your two-stage numeric-residual design, not a differentiator.

ADDITIVE TWO-CHANNEL (SEMANTIC + NUMERIC) UTILITY with the numeric channel carrying most of the load. Documented in auto-bidding (2026) with the explicit conclusion that LLM embeddings 'cannot replace numerical features'.
LINEAR PROBES ON FROZEN LM EMBEDDINGS as a strong baseline for behavioural prediction. AlphaRec (ICLR 2025 Oral) shows a linear map beats ID-based CF. Any nonlinear composition must beat this.

PERSONALIZED / USER-CONDITIONED WEIGHTS OVER AN INTERPRETABLE BASIS, and attention/salience over generated items. Present across LLM-CBM and LLM-recsys work; the intervention interface that discounts specific concepts is already described in 2025 CBM papers.

REPORTING THAT LLM-GENERATED FEATURES ARE SHALLOW RESTATEMENTS. Not a finding you can claim: ELF-Gym (CIKM 2024) quantified the overlap gap, and Küken et al. (2024) documented the operator-simplicity bias.
genuinely_open: No published work tests whether LLM-generated text is a LOSSLESS-PLUS function of its prompt in an information-theoretic sense. Every control found is a performance-difference control (does accuracy drop). Nobody estimates I(Y ; text | tabular fields) or fits an explicit decomposition separating 'recoverable from the prompt' from 'injected by pretraining'. Searches for conditional-mutual-information evaluation of generated features returned nothing in this space. This is the real open slot and the strongest available angle for a NEW METHOD rather than a new architecture.

The controls that exist are almost entirely BINARY (LLM text versus template, versus random). Nobody has proposed a CONTINUOUS measure of how much of a generated text's predictive value is attributable to restating inputs versus injecting pretrained knowledge — e.g. an orthogonalisation or partialling-out estimator that projects narrative embeddings onto the span of the template embeddings and evaluates only the residual component. Orthogonalisation of LLM text against its own tabular source appears unpublished.

In DISCRETE CHOICE specifically, no matched-information control exists at all. The transportation LLM papers (Transportation Science 2025, TRR 2025, arXiv 2508.17527) all compare against classical DCMs, never against a template rendering of the same attributes. Being first to import the control into random-utility modelling is a legitimate methodological contribution even though the control is not itself novel — but it must be framed as transfer plus a formal result, not invention.

Whether LLM-generated PERCEIVED OUTCOMES (counterfactual future consequences) behave differently from LLM-generated DESCRIPTIONS (restatements of present attributes). All prior controls target descriptive expansion. Nothing tests text that is prospective and first-person. This is the only place your framing is genuinely unoccupied — but it requires an experiment that separates the two, e.g. the same K sentences generated in descriptive versus consequence mode, matched for length and count, with the descriptive condition as the control arm.

How to attribute gains in ADDITIVE MULTI-CHANNEL utility models when channels are trained jointly. The auto-bidding paper and your own reviewer both note the numeric channel dominates, but no published method decomposes the joint gain into per-channel contributions (Shapley over channels, or a sequential-orthogonalisation protocol where each channel only sees the residual of the previous). Your 'amplified observed-attribute channel' problem has no standard solution in the literature — proposing one would be a real contribution.

Whether the interpretable structure recovered by LLM-basis bottlenecks is FAITHFUL. 'If Concept Bottlenecks are the Question' (2026) shows concept accuracy and concept quality decorrelate, and 'There Was Never a Bottleneck' (2025) shows leakage defeats the bottleneck claim. No accepted intervention-based faithfulness test exists for LLM-proposed bases in a utility model. Note this also means your Section 3.2 'representational containment' claim is contradicted by Eq. 7's bypass channel and will be flagged.

Identifiability of salience versus personal weights versus semantic scores in a product-form factorisation. Your own ablation record shows the personalised weights collapse in the mixture; no literature establishes conditions under which such a factorisation is identified from choice data alone. A short identifiability analysis would be genuinely new and would convert an embarrassing ablation into a theoretical result.

Contamination-aware evaluation for CHOICE datasets. Bordt et al. covers tabular benchmarks; nothing covers whether an LLM's narrative about an Amazon product leaks co-purchase or rating structure memorised from pretraining. An adapted contamination test for choice-set data is unoccupied.

WaffleCLIP (ICCV 2023) showed random words match LLM descriptors. LangPTune (2024) ran the exact 'raw metadata instead of LLM profile' control and the LLM profile LOST. Random-embedding controls are routine at KDD and RecSys. Placebo-information controls date to CHI 2019. If you present 'we introduce a template control' as a contribution, a reviewer will cite TabLLM and the framing will backfire. CONSEQUENTLY: do not angle the revision as 'new method = architecture'. The architecture (LLM expands records, embed, score on a prompt-defined basis, personalized weights, salience attention, additive semantic+numeric utility) is a recombination of components each individually published 2023-2026 — the reviewer's first point is correct and cannot be argued away. Angle it instead as a new IDENTIFICATION METHOD for outcome-mediated signal. The genuinely open slot, verified empty across all searches, is that every existing control is a binary performance-difference check; nobody has an estimator that decomposes a generated text's predictive value into the part recoverable from the prompt and the part injected by the model, and nobody has a principled way to attribute gains across channels in an additive multi-channel utility model. On baselines, the two concrete gaps a reviewer can name are AlphaRec-style linear probe on the same frozen embeddings (ICLR 2025 Oral) and the persona-based embedding method in Transportation Science 2025 on Swissmetro, which you already have an adapter for. papers.title: Generalized random utility model
papers.relevance: Walker & Ben-Akiva. The formal GRUM: structural equations linking latent variables to observables, measurement equations linking latent variables to indicators, and the identification conditions required (scale and location normalisation of latent constructs, order and rank conditions).

Recast V_tj = E_o[u(o,z)] as a GRUM with a structural equation o* = h(z,c,x) + omega and a measurement equation (narrative embeddings) = Lambda o* + nu. Written this way the identification obligations become explicit and the reviewer's 'is this just semantic expansion' question becomes a testable normalisation question rather than a rhetorical one.

If the Amazon gains come from the amplified observed-attribute channel, an L-MNL with the same observed features and a learned residual is the correct control. Run it. If L-MNL matches OM-LEU on Amazon, the outcome channel is not carrying the result and the paper must say so.

papers.title: Deep neural networks for choice analysis: Architecture design with alternative-specific utility functions
papers.venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies, 112, 234-251
papers.relevance: Wang, Mo, Zhao. ASU-DNN constrains each alternative's utility to depend only on that alternative's own attributes, reducing estimation error versus a fully connected DNN and yielding more regular substitution patterns.
papers.implication: Already cited. Establishes that imposing utility-theoretic architectural structure on a neural choice model is standard practice, not a contribution. Also the right place to check whether OM-LEU's outcome channel respects alternative-specific separability; if the salience mechanism looks across alternatives, IIA and substitution-pattern behaviour need reporting.

papers.title: RUMBoost: Gradient boosted random utility models
papers.venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies, 170, 104897
papers.relevance: Salvade & Hillel. Replaces each utility parameter with a constrained ensemble of regression trees, enforcing monotone marginal utilities and alternative-specific attributes, giving an intrinsically interpretable non-linear utility learned from data; extends to nested and mixed specifications.
papers.implication: Already cited, and the strongest tabular-only baseline available. Because it is intrinsically interpretable AND high-capacity, it removes the 'interpretability versus flexibility tradeoff' framing that OM-LEU's introduction leans on (lines 37-44). Rewrite that framing and report RUMBoost on the observed features for both datasets; if RUMBoost closes most of the Amazon gap, the honest claim shrinks and the paper is stronger for saying so first.

papers.title: Synthesizing Attitudes, Predicting Actions (SAPA): Behavioral Theory-Guided LLMs for Ridesourcing Mode Choice Modeling
papers.relevance: Prompts an LLM to generate traveler personas from raw survey data, then to produce QUANTITATIVE SCORES for a predefined set of latent attitudes (the Technology Acceptance Model supplying a Tech Affinity construct), feeding a downstream propensity model. Reports up to 75.9% PR-AUC improvement.
papers.implication: Prior art for 'LLM generates scores on a theory-defined latent basis which then drive a choice model', roughly 12 months before a NeurIPS 2026 submission, and uncited. This is the concrete thing behind reviewer concern 1. Cite it and state the delta precisely: SAPA scores INDIVIDUAL-specific attitudes from survey data; OM-LEU scores ALTERNATIVE-specific perceived outcomes from alternative metadata and composes them inside a decomposable RUM rather than a propensity model. That is a real difference, but only if stated.

papers.title: Personalized Decision Modeling: Utility Optimization or Textualized-Symbolic Reasoning
papers.relevance: Zhao, Zhao, Du, Yang. ATHENA: LLM-augmented symbolic discovery of group-level utility functions, then per-individual semantic adaptation guided by the discovered utility; evaluated on travel mode and vaccine choice; ablations show both stages are needed.
papers.implication: Second uncited 2025 prior art in the same LLM-plus-utility-plus-personalisation space. Together with SAPA it means that combination is now a populated area, so a 2026 novelty claim must narrow to the outcome-mediation structure itself plus its identification evidence.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Travel Behavior Prediction
papers.relevance: Zero-shot prompting of an LLM with task description, individual attributes and domain knowledge; reaches accuracy comparable to classical discrete choice models and ML classifiers.
papers.implication: The baseline reviewers will ask for and the paper does not appear to run on its own datasets: a direct LLM predictor with no utility structure. If a zero-shot or few-shot LLM ranker matches OM-LEU's NLL, the architecture is not earning its complexity. If it does not, that gap is a clean argument for the structure.

papers.title: Large Language Models Predict Transportation Mode Choice Behavior for a Variety of Alternative Sets
papers.venue: Transportation Research Record: Journal of the Transportation Research Board (SAGE), DOI 10.1177/03611981251352499
papers.relevance: Nishida, Ishigaki, Onishi. Language-based mode choice model where alternatives and variables are rendered as sentences and the output token names the chosen mode; shown more versatile than MNL across varying alternative sets.
papers.implication: Evidence that rendering structured alternatives as natural language and letting an LLM choose is established practice, published in a choice venue. Strengthens the need for OM-LEU to show its gain is not merely 'text rendering of tabular features helps', which is exactly the semantic-expansion hypothesis in reviewer concern 2.

papers.title: Promises and Pitfalls of Black-Box Concept Learning Models
papers.venue: arXiv:2106.13314; ICML 2021 Workshop on Theoretic Foundation, Criticism and Application Trend of Explainable AI
papers.relevance: Mahinpei, Clark, Lage, Doshi-Velez, Pan. Concept representations encode information beyond the predefined concepts; natural mitigations do not fully work; downstream interpretation is therefore misleading. This is the leakage result OM-LEU cites at line 89.
papers.implication: The paper's rebuttal to leakage ('each u_m output is a scalar utility, not a vector embedding') is too quick and a reviewer will catch it. A scalar bottleneck restricts per-concept channel capacity but does not prevent M scalars from jointly encoding off-basis information, especially when scores are learned jointly with the choice objective. The defensible version is an empirical leakage measurement: probe the concatenated scores for observed attributes they should not contain, and report the result.

papers.title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
papers.venue: Proceedings of EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019, pages 2733-2743, Hong Kong (ACL Anthology D19-1275)
papers.relevance: Hewitt & Liang. Introduces SELECTIVITY: a probe is evidence about a representation only if it achieves high task accuracy AND low accuracy on a control task with randomised labels. Complex probes memorise regardless of what the representation encodes.
papers.implication: The cleanest transplantable answer to reviewer concern 2. Build the control: generate narratives from SHUFFLED or ATTRIBUTE-ABLATED metadata (same LLM, same prompt, same embedding pipeline, wrong item) and refit. If OM-LEU's NLL gain survives the control, the gain comes from fluent text plus model capacity, not from perceived outcomes of THIS alternative. If it collapses, that collapse is the identification evidence the paper currently lacks, and it is cheap to run.

papers.title: A General Approach to Causal Mediation Analysis
papers.relevance: Imai, Keele, Tingley. Average causal mediation effects are nonparametrically identified under sequential ignorability; the paper also supplies sensitivity analysis for violations of that assumption.
papers.implication: 'Mediated' in OM-LEU's title is a causal-mediation word with a precise technical meaning and a known identification assumption the paper never invokes, tests or satisfies. Two options: add a sensitivity analysis in this spirit for the outcome layer, or rename the method to something non-causal (outcome-CONDITIONED or consequence-BASIS utility). Leaving a causal word attached to a purely predictive architecture is a gift to a hostile reviewer.

papers.title: Integrated choice and latent variable models: A literature review on mode choice
papers.venue: GAEL Working Paper 2018-07, Grenoble Applied Economics Laboratory (hal-01795630)
papers.relevance: Bouscasse. Systematic review of ICLV applications to mode choice covering specification, estimation and the recurring identification problems.
papers.implication: Efficient single citation for 'this is a large, mature literature' in the related-work paragraph that currently does not exist. Also a source of candidate applications for positioning the Mobility-Boston result against published ICLV mode-choice findings.

already_standard: Utility computed over latent perceived constructs rather than raw observed attributes. Established by Ben-Akiva et al. (2002) and Walker & Ben-Akiva (2002). The abstract's claim that 'most discrete choice models do not explicitly represent this perceptual layer' is inaccurate as written and is likely the single sentence that triggered reviewer concern 1.

The distinction between individual-specific latent constructs (attitudes) and alternative-specific latent constructs (perceptions), the latter being exactly what OM-LEU calls perceived outcomes. Bahamonde-Birke et al. (2017).
Person-conditional taste parameters produced by a neural network inside an otherwise interpretable utility. TasteNet-MNL, Han et al. (TR-B 2022). OM-LEU itself concedes this at line 75.

Splitting utility into a knowledge-driven interpretable term and a learned data-driven term. L-MNL, Sifringer et al. (TR-B 2020) - architecturally the same two-channel design OM-LEU uses, six years earlier.

Imposing utility-theoretic architectural constraints on a neural choice model (alternative-specific separability, monotonicity, sign restrictions). ASU-DNN (Wang et al., TR-C 2020) and RUMBoost (Salvade & Hillel, TR-C 2025).

Intrinsically interpretable non-linear utility learned from data with monotonicity guarantees. RUMBoost. This removes the interpretability-versus-flexibility tradeoff that OM-LEU's introduction is built on.
Rendering structured choice alternatives as natural-language sentences and having an LLM predict the choice. Nishida et al. (TRR 2025); Mo et al. (arXiv:2312.00819).

Prompting an LLM to emit scores on a predefined, theory-grounded latent basis and feeding those scores to a downstream choice or propensity model. SAPA (arXiv:2509.18181, Sept 2025) - the closest single piece of prior art, and uncited.
LLM-augmented discovery of a utility function plus per-individual semantic adaptation. ATHENA (arXiv:2511.02194, Nov 2025) - also uncited.
Concept-bottleneck architectures with named intermediate concepts, and the documented leakage problem in them. Koh et al. and Mahinpei et al., both already in the paper's bibliography.

Sequential (two-stage) estimation of a latent-construct choice model and its known inference penalty. Raveau et al. (TRR 2010); Bahamonde-Birke & Ortuzar (TRR 2014). OM-LEU's cached-narrative pipeline is a sequential estimator and should say so.

The idea that a latent-variable choice model's fit improvement is not evidence of the latent construct. Settled by Vij & Walker (2016); treating NLL as the identification argument is the opposite of current practice.
genuinely_open: Whether a latent perceptual construct can be identified WITHOUT survey indicators. Every ICLV measurement equation in the field is anchored to human-reported Likert items. OM-LEU's narratives come from an LLM that was itself conditioned on the alternative's observed attributes, so the measurement channel is endogenous to the structural channel in a way ICLV never contemplated. Nobody has solved this. Stating it as THE open problem, and offering LLM narratives as a candidate instrument plus the tests that would falsify them, is a far stronger and more defensible contribution than claiming the perceptual layer is new.

What exclusion restriction can make an LLM-derived perceptual construct separable from the observed attributes it was generated from. ICLV gets separation because indicators (survey responses) are a different data source from the choice; OM-LEU has one data source. Candidate restrictions worth trying: generate narratives from a STRICT SUBSET of attributes and withhold the rest for the observed channel; or use person-side context in the narrative prompt that never enters the observed channel. Either gives a real exclusion restriction and turns the architecture into a claim that can be tested rather than asserted. This also directly answers reviewer concern 3 about the amplified observed-attribute channel.

Whether LLM-generated perceived-outcome scores agree with human-reported perceptions of the same alternatives. Directly measurable and currently absent. A small human-annotation study, or reuse of STAMP-standardised items on a dataset that has them, would answer reviewer concern 2 empirically instead of rhetorically. Highest-value single experiment available.

How much of an LLM-text gain is semantic expansion versus genuine perceptual content. The control-task methodology (Hewitt & Liang 2019) gives a template nobody has applied in discrete choice: refit on narratives generated from shuffled or attribute-ablated inputs and measure selectivity. Being first to run this in choice modelling is itself a contribution.

Whether Vij & Walker's reduction result extends to neural and LLM-mediated latent channels. Their proof concerns classical ICLV specifications. Whether an equivalent latent-free model always exists that matches an LLM-mediated model appears unanswered. Proving or empirically probing this for OM-LEU's model class would be a genuine theoretical contribution and would convert the paper's biggest vulnerability into its main result.

Practical identifiability of high-dimensional prompt-defined semantic bases. Raveau et al. (2012) established that low-dimensional hybrid choice models are already empirically fragile; a basis of many LLM-scored semantic axes is far worse conditioned. The needed normalisations (scale, location, rotation of the semantic basis) are not worked out anywhere. Working them out would explain and fix the hyperparameter sensitivity in reviewer concern 4.

Whether a perceived-outcome channel survives competition with a full set of alternative-specific constants. Bahamonde-Birke et al. (2017) show perceptions absorb ASC variance; this test has not been run for LLM-derived perceptions and is the sharpest available version of reviewer concern 3 on Amazon.

Reproducibility norms for prompt-derived latent constructs. The field has just proposed a standard measurement protocol for survey-based subjective variables (STAMP, Transportation 2024); there is no analogue for prompt-based ones. Full prompts, LLM version pinning, decoding temperature, embedding model and seed-to-seed stability of the recovered basis are all unaddressed in the literature, and the paper is being marked down (reviewer concern 4) for exactly this gap. Proposing the protocol is a contribution the field currently wants.

Direction of effect between generated 'perceived outcomes' and choice in cross-sectional data. Mehdizadeh et al. (Transport Reviews 2026) show the cross-sectional/longitudinal gap is real and large; no LLM-mediated choice model has addressed it. A temporal split where narratives are generated from period-t metadata and evaluated on period-t+1 choices would be a first step and is cheap given the existing temporal-split infrastructure.
